Mahābhārata
by Vedavyāsa alias Kṛṣṇadvaipāyaṇa. in 18 Parvans viz., Ādi, Sabhā, Vana (Āraṇya), Virāṭa, Udyoga, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Karṇa, Śalya, Sauptika, Strī, Śānti, Anuśāsana, Aśvamedha, Āśramavāsa, Mausala, Mahāprasthāna, Svargārohaṇa an. 100 Upaparvans (Anukramaṅikā to Bhaviṣyatparvan). [Page19-100a]
For a critical analysis of the contents of the three stages an. a final fourth stage in the development of the epic, see Bhāratasaṃhitā or Ur Mahābhārata, Intro. p.. VI-XII. Redactor. D.. Keshavram R. Shastree, Gujarat Res. Soc. Ahmedabad, 1998.
For a study of the development of Mahābhārata from its Primeval Introgermane home to its present form, see, Adolf Holtzmann: Zur Geschichte an. Kritik des Mahābhārata, Keil, 1892.
For southern recension of the text an. alphabetical index of names, see T. R. Krishnamacharya edn. N. S. Press, Bombay: Kumbhakonam, 1912-14.
For a detailed study on this epic on several aspects like date, details of dh. science an. its development into final form, see Kane, HDS. I. ii. p.. 349-85.
For Upaparvan reference, see V. S. Sukthankar, The Mahābhārata Ādiparvan, v.. 1.2.33-1.2.69. Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, Poona, 1933.
On the allocation of the Upaparvans in the main parvans acc. to Arjunamiśra (Commentator) an. Mahābhārata Anukramaṇī (verses 311-58), see Brockhaus, Del 100 Parva des Mahābhārata, ZDMG. VI (1852). 528-32.
For details of the northern an. southern recensions of the text an. mss. ref., see V. S. Sukthankar, The Mahābhārata Ādiparvan, Prolegomena, p.. xxxi-xxxiv.
Analysis of text is based on BORI. edn. [Page19-100b]
